name: adbc
description: Attach an ADBC database as a DuckDB catalog with table discovery, supported projection/filter pushdown, and Arrow result streams. The alias is also the first argument of every adbc_* function; DETACH disconnects. BEGIN … COMMIT groups catalog writes with adbc_execute and adbc_insert, and READ_ONLY rejects all of them. CALL adbc_clear_cache refreshes metadata after remote DDL. Pass http(s) URIs (e.g. Trino) as the uri option rather than the ATTACH path, which DuckDB would treat as a remote file.

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: Driver name resolved through installed manifests, or shared-library path. Required unless supplied by a secret or profile.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: Connection URI passed to the driver, overriding the ATTACH path. Use it for `http://`/`https://` URIs.

parameters.name: entrypoint
parameters.description: Custom driver entrypoint function name. Only needed for drivers that don't follow the standard `AdbcDriverInit` symbol convention.

parameters.name: search_paths
parameters.description: Extra colon-separated directories to look in for ADBC driver manifests (`*.toml`) and connection profiles, in addition to the platform defaults.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Name of an ADBC connection profile supplying the driver and options. Equivalent to an ATTACH path of `profile://<name>`.

parameters.name: use_manifests
parameters.description: Set to `'false'` to skip manifest resolution entirely (load the driver only by absolute path).

parameters.name: batch_size
parameters.description: Hint for the number of rows per Arrow batch when scanning. Larger values reduce per-batch overhead at the cost of memory.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: Name of an ADBC secret containing driver and connection options. Without it, a secret whose scope prefixes the ATTACH path's URI is used automatically.

examples.description: Attach a SQLite file, then commit and roll back remote writes
Attach PostgreSQL for analytics (requires a configured database and authentication)
Read an existing SQLite application database (replace the path)
Attach through a connection profile (requires mydb.toml in a profile search path)
